speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a neonate presenting with seizures and lethargy three days after birth; can you confirm if your mother had any infections during pregnancy or if you were born prematurely?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, Blood_Culture, Glucose, Calcium, Magnesium, Ammonia.

speaker: Doctor
text: The initial metabolic and infectious workup came back with normal readings. Given your history of seizures and lethargy, have you or your mother noticed any jaundice, or did you receive a blood transfusion shortly after birth?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
You are a very low birth weight preterm infant born to a mother with chorioamnionitis, with Apgar scores of 3 and 6. Given your history of seizures, lethargy, and poor initial condition, have you received any phototherapy, and does your mother have a history of GBS infection?

REQUEST TEST: Serum Bilirubin, Blood Culture (Repeat), Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE) secondary to perinatal asphyxia in a very low birth weight infant, with chorioamnionitis as a contributing factor. The clinical picture of seizures, lethargy, low Apgar scores, and maternal chorioamnionitis strongly supports this diagnosis despite the normal initial metabolic panel.
